contexts.text: Forty days and nights = the duration of temptation.
That the Earth will not last to eternity. Signified, Explained.
Duration and state. Signified. AC 1341. AC 1344. AC 1346.
Four hundred years = the duration and state of temptation.
The fourth generation = the same as the fortieth and the four hundredth, namely, the duration and state of temptation.
He was in the house of the prison = the duration of temptation... To be in it = to stay there, thus duration.
Ye shall not leave of it until the morning = the duration of this state before a state of enlightenment in Heaven.
The dwelling of the Sons of Israel in which they dwelt in Egypt = the duration of infestations.
A year, like all things belonging to time, = state and its duration.
An age = duration even to the end; and, in the internal sense, by this duration is signified what is eternal. Illustrated.
It came to pass the day following = the duration of such worship, even to the end of the Church.
There is no fixed term of their continuance there.
This first state of man after death lasts with some for days, with some for months, and with some for a year, but rarely beyond that with anyone.
That this New Church... will last for ever and ever...
The less coherent a thing is, or the less it resembles a solid, the more durable it is...
Forty years, also = the whole duration of temptation.
